propositions: The plan-review gate's LLM-as-judge must exhibit self-consistency: the same finding re-judged must produce the same Pass-3 decision across multiple runs, with Fleiss' κ ≥ 0.6 and raw agreement ≥ 0.8 as the pass floor.

Section-order permutation of plan input must not flip the final gate verdict; order-shuffle stability is measured over 14 plans with ≥3 top-level sections across 3 distinct permutations each, gated by κ ≥ 0.6 and raw agreement ≥ 0.8.

Infra-level INDETERMINATE verdicts (those carrying llm_unavailable or verify_failed coverage flags) are execution failures and must be excluded and re-run; only genuine judge-indeterminate outcomes (neither flag set) are retained as an agreement category.

E6 is a measurement experiment on the existing gate (no src/rebar code changes); it gates R5 (via self-consistency pass) and R3 (via order-shuffle pass) and provides stability attestation before new sub-answer vocabulary is added.

Experiment A tests self-consistency of Pass-2/Pass-3 over N=50 findings from the G6/E4/T3 cohort (rows filtered from adjudication_corpus.jsonl) with 3 votes per finding; Experiment B tests order-shuffle stability over 14 permutable plans from corpus_sample.json with 3 distinct section permutations each.

LLM-spend is bounded and honest: Exp A = 150 agentic Pass-2 calls (50 findings × 3 votes), Exp B = 42 full-gate runs (14 plans × 3 permutations); the harness drives only the public review_plan entrypoint with frozen committed inputs and no production-store mutations.
